record.title: GUI burst open treats failed container-side collection as success (empty baseline or no burst) with no audit record
record.description: When the first agent GUI input of a burst arrives, AgentBox._snapshot takes a docker-commit snapshot and then calls _open_gui_burst. That method collects the /workspace manifest and the desktop process baseline. Two silent fail-open paths exist. (a) Exit status unchecked (the path observed live): SandboxManager.workspace_manifest runs the root `find ... | head -c` exec and returns `_parse_manifest(res.output[0] or b"")` without checking res.exit_code. If the in-container command cannot run, it returns ({}, False) with no exception, and _open_gui_burst records the burst against an empty baseline. desktop_processes and kill_processes ignore exit status in the same way. At close, the diff reports every pre-existing file as added. The audit event carries counts and truncated=True plus only the first 100 sorted paths, so the real GUI-made change can fall outside the listed paths, and nothing records that the baseline collection failed. Parent-live l7 measured this on agentbox-desktop:0.1 with the desktop pids cgroup at 1022-1024/1024: the manifest had 0 entries, the burst was recorded, the audit showed only tool_request/policy_decision/snapshot/tool_result, and close gave gui_changes added=301 with truncated=True while the real change zz_changed_by_gui.txt was absent from the listed 100. (b) Exception swallowed: if either collector raises, the bare `except Exception: return` at service.py:210 records no burst. Later GUI inputs inside the idle/interval window open no new burst, so there is no stray kill and no gui_changes for that window. The same pattern at :221 and :238 skips the kill or the diff at close. A mock reproduces this, but no agent-reachable raising trigger is known: it needs a Docker API error such as the container gone or not running, or the docker client's 60 s read timeout. Correction to the hunter's plan: pid pressure does not reach :210. It reaches the unchecked-exit path (a). Bounds: the burst snapshot is still taken and logged, so the restore point survives. In the measured pid-pressure case ps still ran, so the stray-kill baseline was populated. gui_changes is a detective, partial control: the GUI is approval-free by design (N-1). Agent reachability, not yet run live: the default policy allows an approval-free exec of `tail -f /dev/null & ` x1000 + `tail -f /dev/null` (rule read-only-exec). It runs as uid 1000, which the stray killer never targets. It holds pids until exec_timeout (60 s), and then GNU timeout's group kill releases them. That gives the agent a self-releasing way to apply pressure while it sends a concurrent GUI input. In the parent experiment the pressure came from direct docker exec as uid 1001, not from the agent API.
record.claimed_root_cause: Burst bookkeeping treats a failed container-side collection as a successful one. workspace_manifest (sandbox.py:499-501), desktop_processes (sandbox.py:689-692) and kill_processes (sandbox.py:697) never check exec exit status, and _open_gui_burst/_stop_gui_strays/_close_gui_burst (service.py:210, 221, 238) swallow every exception. In both cases there is no audit event and no fail-closed fallback, such as refusing further GUI input or marking the burst baseline invalid.

trace.description: Agent token (lowest-trust principal, own sandbox) sends a GUI input tool (key/click/type). Policy default is allow, with no approval.
On an allowed GUI input that starts a burst (_gui_needs_snapshot true), it calls _snapshot.
After docker commit, it opens the GUI burst with the new snapshot id.
Root find exec result is parsed without checking exit_code. A failed exec (e.g. no free pid in the cgroup) returns ({}, False) instead of raising.

Burst is recorded with the empty manifest as its baseline, with no audit event marking the collection as failed. The later gui_changes diff therefore reports all existing files as added and can leave the real change out of the 100 listed paths.

evidence.description: except Exception: return in _open_gui_burst. A raising collector leaves no burst and no audit record.
except Exception: return in _stop_gui_strays. A failed ps/xdotool/kill skips the stray kill silently.
except Exception: return in _close_gui_burst. A failed close-time manifest skips gui_changes silently.
gui_changes lists only v[:100] of each sorted diff list plus counts and a truncated flag, so an empty baseline buries the real change.
desktop_processes ignores the ps exit status. A failed exec yields an empty process list.
kill_processes ignores the kill exec's exit status.
read-only-exec allow rule includes tail. simple_programs treats & as a separator, so a 1000-way background `tail -f /dev/null` exec is approval-free.
Live: under pid pressure, workspace_manifest returned 0 entries with no exception.
Live: first GUI input still 200, burst recorded with baseline manifest entries 0.
Live: after pressure ends, the next GUI input opens no new burst (needs_snapshot False), so the degraded burst persists.
Live: close gives gui_changes added=301, truncated=True, and the real change is not in the listed 100 paths. Control at line 3 shows added=1 with the change listed.
Mock: a raising workspace_manifest at open leaves no burst. Lines 3-5 show only the snapshot event, no new burst on the next input, no kill, no gui_changes.

Real SandboxManager collectors with a fake container whose exec exits 126: workspace_manifest returns ({}, False), desktop_processes returns ([], set()), and kill_processes returns, all without raising.
Real _close_gui_burst with an empty baseline: counts added=301, truncated=True, real change not listed. The control on line 15 lists it.
Default policy decides allow (read-only-exec) for `tail -f /dev/null & ` x1000 + `tail -f /dev/null`.

Under the same `timeout -k 5 T bash -c` wrapper as SandboxManager.exec, the background tails are killed at timeout (zombies only because the harness's PID 1 does not reap), so the pressure releases itself after exec_timeout.

blockers: Not observed on the live image: whether the approval-free agent-API sequence keeps the desktop container's pids cgroup at its 1024 limit while a concurrent first GUI input makes the root find at sandbox.py:499-501 return empty. The sequence is an allowlisted exec of `tail -f /dev/null & ` x~1000 + `tail -f /dev/null` (uid 1000, which the stray killer does not target) with a concurrent GUI input such as key shift. The GUI input must still return 200, and the pressure must then release at exec_timeout. Parent-live l7 showed the empty-baseline effect only with pressure created by direct docker exec as uid 1001, and this verifier has no Docker access.

No agent-reachable trigger is identified for the exception path at service.py:210/221/238 (a Docker API error, a container not running, or the docker client's 60 s read timeout during collection). This path stays mock-only.

validation_plan.local: Parent-live, Docker-backed, disposable desktop sandbox, dummy human/agent tokens, scratch AGENTBOX_HOME, loopback only. Delete the sandbox afterwards. (1) As the agent token, create 300 files under /workspace with allowlisted calls (write_file, or exec `touch f1.txt ... f300.txt`), then wait > gui_snapshot_idle. (2) In a background thread, as the agent token, POST tools/exec {command: 'tail -f /dev/null & ' * 1000 + 'tail -f /dev/null'}. Expect policy_decision allow / read-only-exec. Poll the container's pids.current from the host until it is >= pids.max - 2. (3) As the agent token, POST tools/key {keys: 'shift'}. Record the status, whether box._gui_burst[sid] exists, the size of its manifest, and the new audit events. (4) Wait for the exec to return (exit 124, pressure released). Using only agent GUI tools (key/type into an Xfce terminal), create /workspace/zz_changed_by_gui.txt. (5) Wait > gui_snapshot_idle, then GET /audit as the human. Expected if the finding holds: the burst has 0 manifest entries, no audit event mentions the collection failure, and gui_changes shows added≈301, truncated=True, with zz_changed_by_gui.txt absent from added. The control run without step 2 must show added=1 with the file listed. Refuted for this agent path if the exec cannot fill the cgroup, the snapshot or GUI input fails with 503, or the manifest is complete. Fix check: workspace_manifest/desktop_processes/kill_processes raise SandboxError on a nonzero exit, and _open_gui_burst/_stop_gui_strays/_close_gui_burst log a gui_burst_error audit event and mark the burst baseline invalid, or require human approval for further GUI input until a burst opens with a good baseline. Rerun steps 1-5 and expect a gui_burst_error event and no silent empty baseline.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on a non-production desktop sandbox: run the same sequence with the deployment's AGENTBOX_DESKTOP_PIDS, AGENTBOX_EXEC_TIMEOUT and AGENTBOX_GUI_SNAPSHOT_IDLE values. Confirm whether the human-facing timeline (web UI audit fragment / CLI) shows any sign that the burst baseline was lost, and whether the GUI-made change is visible without restoring the burst snapshot.
